Subject: QBR prep: GPU econ sprint commitments & capacity playbook

Team —

We need a tight packet for the QBR focused on capacity planning and GPU unit economics. High level ask: provide an operational-ready snapshot we can put into the leadership deck by EOD Fri (May 24). Specifically please include:

- A 12-week GPU spend forecast (monthly cadence) with committed vs. spot split. (I attached a template: 2028-05-22-gpu-spend-forecast.xlsx)
- Current utilization by queue/model family (p50/p95 token latency and avg GPU occupancy).
- Explicit delta analysis for batching and KV/prefix caching improvements we ran in the last sprint (cost savings, latency impact, risk).
- Any open procurement/term constraints (billing windows, minimum commit).

I want a short one-slide recommendation: 1) Recommended commit level for Dedicated (month vs year), 2) Short list of three actions to reduce unit cost with estimated $/token impact, and 3) Runway risk (weeks) if traffic grows +30%.

Attachments: 2028-05-22-gpu-spend-forecast.xlsx

Thanks — concise bullets are better than long narratives. I will consolidate and draft the leadership talking points on Saturday.

Irene Choi
Head, Infrastructure Planning
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: 2028-05-22-gpu-spend-forecast.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

Subject: Re: QBR prep: GPU econ sprint commitments & capacity playbook

Irene — thanks, great template. Sending preliminary numbers and the experimental summary. Key points up front:

- Short answer on commit: recommend 3-month tiered commit for burst smoothing + a 12% reserved pool for enterprise customers. Yearly commit only if legal can compress the cancellation window below 60 days.
- Forecast (attached xlsx): May/Jun/Jul projected spend (hosted + dedicated) with expected 22% uplift in token volume in Jun. If we do the batching/cache changes, net unit cost reduction ~17% by July.
- Utilization: p50 latency steady; p95 shows tail degradation on long-context chat workloads; occupancy average across prod GPU fleet = 64% (current), with peaks at 91% for some critical routes.
- Batching/cache experiments (attached pdf): caching prefix hits moved from 18% -> 46% on sampled chat load; that alone yields ~8–10% token-cost savings; combined with adaptive batching and micro-batching it reaches ~17%. Latency tradeoff: median unaffected, p95 improves slightly but some workloads see +10–30ms due to batching window.

I've attached: 1) updated gpu-spend spreadsheet, 2) batching-cache-experiments-summary.pdf.

Karthik
Director, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: gpu-spend-forecast-populated.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

Quick operational read:

TL;DR: Prioritize caching improvements + 3-month commit; hold off on large yearly commit until we validate tail-latency regressions on long-context production flows.

Notes:
- Reserve vs spot: spot remains a good lever for non-SLA traffic; however, for enterprise plans we should lock 12–15% reserved to avoid throttles during peak launches.
- Canary/fallback: add an automatic fallback to a lower-capacity but compatible model family when p95 queue wait > 300ms — this preserves availability at the cost of some quality. Operations can ship this rule within 48 hours.
- Risk: if traffic +30% within 6 weeks we hit saturation on the eu-west pool first; US pool has 3–4 weeks runway with current burst provisioning.
- Cost tradeoffs: caching fixes are the fastest win (~8–12% cost saving) because they reduce decoding tokens. Batching gives another ~5% but has the most variance by workload. Quantization experiments so far help in internal testbeds but need more regression checks for customer-facing models.

I'll add these bullets to the ops appendix for the deck. Assigning owners: SRE will own the canary routing work (I can coordinate), Karthik will finalize the cost deltas and slides, Lauren please prepare the one-slide exec recommendation.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Infrastructure & Operations
Redwood Inference
